English translation from the Modern Amharic of the EOTC Bible (nehemiah-osc.org) by Claude (Anthropic) with collaborator, May 2026. Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication (archive.org/details/three-books-of-meqabyan-cc0-translation). Apparatus integrates Josef Horovitz, 'Das äthiopische Maccabäerbuch,' Zeitschrift für Assyriologie XIX (1905), pp. 194-233 — PD primary scholarly study. 64-citation third-pass audit verdict matrix; 57 verified, 4 errors corrected, 3 interpretive readings flagged, 7 newly discovered parallels added. Dating widened to Aksumite-to-Solomonic Ethiopian Christian range (4th-14th c. CE); precise composition date undetermined in current scholarship per Horovitz 1905 non-commitment. Three books: 1 Mq 36 chapters (Maqabis-of-Benjamin martyrology vs Ṣiruṣaydan); 2 Mq 21 chapters (Maqabis-of-Moab conversion + sons' martyrdom + Ṣiruṣaydan's death); 3 Mq 10 chapters (homiletic + angelological dialogue + Satan-refused-Adam tradition + resurrection-doctrine).

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) Third Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan III) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 8 — HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR (per source-fidelity note). Ch 8 likely develops PREPARATION FOR DEATH + REPENTANCE-AS-LIFE-PROCESS completing the complete-repentance doctrinal arc (seed 4:34's four-step rubric extended over a lifetime rather than compressed into a single act). The preparation-for-death theme parallels: HEBREWS 9:27 ('it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment'); SIRACH 7:36 ('whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss'); WISDOM 4:10-15 (the righteous-quickly-translated death); LATER MEDIEVAL ARS MORIENDI tradition; THE WISDOM-LITERATURE death-and-judgment integration. Tewahedo monastic-tradition preserves the memento-mori (REMEMBER-DEATH) theme as the daily-meditation rubric. The Mäṣḥafä Mäwet (Book of Death) is the canonical-Tewahedo funerary-and-preparation-for-death liturgical text drawing on this preparation-for-death theology.

HOMILETIC-GENRE ANCHOR — likely development of FINAL-CONFESSION theme (deathbed-confession preparation). The deathbed-confession tradition parallels: LUKE 23:39-43 (the good-thief's deathbed-confession — 'Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom'); ACTS 7:54-60 (Stephen's deathbed-prayer + commendation-of-spirit); CHRYSOSTOM Homilies on Penitence 1 (the deathbed-confession-as-valid theology); GREGORY OF NYSSA In Suam Ordinationem; AMBROSE Letter 38 (on Maximus's deathbed-confession). The Tewahedo sacramental tradition preserves the deathbed-confession as VALID-WITH-IMMEDIATE-ABSOLUTION pending the Fetha Nagast canonical-stipulations. The verse-position likely articulates the EOTC doctrine that the complete-repentance four-step rubric (4:34) can compress to a single-deathbed-act under genuine-contrition + verbal-confession + tear-of-repentance + intention-of-non-return.
